failed_valid_items.subject: accountancy
failure_details: Average period formula = (Months remaining after first drawing + Months remaining after last drawing) / 2.
(A) End of each half year: (6 + 0) / 2 = 3 months, matching (IV).
(B) Beginning of each quarter: (12 + 3) / 2 = 7.5 months, matching (III).
(C) Beginning of each month: (12 + 1) / 2 = 6.5 months, matching (II).
(D) End of each quarter: (9 + 0) / 2 = 4.5 months, matching (I).
Thus, the correct combination is (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I), corresponding to Option D.

failed_valid_items.subject: economics
failure_details: The textbook definition directly supports D: greater thrift leaves total saving unchanged or lower (E1.1); its worked example shows aggregate saving unchanged after equilibrium income falls (E1.2–E1.5).

A is also defensible in the standard two-sector equilibrium: if aggregate saving does not rise and saving equals investment, investment does not rise either. The stem gives no assumption that rules out this equivalent implication, so D is not uniquely defensible.

B and C reverse the thrift increase in the definition; they do not state the paradox’s defining cause. Under fixed autonomous investment, however, aggregate saving can remain unchanged for those changes too, so the model context is underspecified.
The item exactly repeats its supplied CUET 2024 anchor, so it is not meaningfully distinct.
